gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power each 'all-in-one' system uses just by being switched on. The Solar Lab measured about 65 W idle for the EG4 FlexBOSS21 and reported about 45 W for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra (its comparison article says roughly 60 W). A Tesla Motors Club owner logged an average standby drain of 72–110 W on a Powerwall 3. That is about 1.1 to 2.6 kWh a day lost before any household load runs.
standout_why: I read the three cited pages. EnergySage (best-batteries-for-whole-home-backup, updated 2026-05-11) gives only quoted specs and scores and no measurements. iTechGuides (Powerwall alternatives, 2026-10-25) gives only spec and Amazon-listing figures and says its efficiency numbers are 'not a uniform laboratory test'. SolutionEnergy /batteries/ says 'we didn't test them'. None of them gives idle or self-consumption draw for any candidate, measured or rated. EnergySage and iTechGuides also list the Powerwall 3 at 97.5% 'roundtrip', but Tesla's own spec page gives 89% for the solar-to-battery-to-home round trip and 97.5% for solar-to-home only. None of the rivals has a measured figure from a named lab.
decides: The finding confirms the ranking but does not overturn it. For a grid-tied home, idle draw of 45–110 W costs about 0.4–1 MWh a year and barely matters. For the off-grid or long-outage buyer that ChatGPT's follow-up question points to, it does matter. By The Solar Lab's numbers, the EG4 FlexBOSS21 (65 W) and the DELTA Pro Ultra (45–60 W) idle lower than the 72–110 W one Powerwall 3 owner logged. The Tesla 89% versus 97.5% correction also narrows the efficiency lead that EnergySage and iTechGuides give the Powerwall 3 over FranklinWH (rated 90% per EnergySage).

findings.label: Idle consumption, measured
findings.value: about 65 W (Sol-Ark 18K: about 108 W in the same test)
findings.source_title: Sol-Ark 18K vs EG4 FlexBOSS21: Which Hybrid Solar Inverter is Best for Your Home? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'The EG4 FlexBOSS 21 consumed about 65 watts during our idle consumption tests.' No setup or duration is described, and the page has no byline or date. 65 W × 24 h = 1.56 kWh/day. This matches EG4's rated idle of <65 W.

findings.label: Idle draw, reported by tester
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X home backup unit (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab says 'the original EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra has around a 45W idle draw' and links to its own testing article. The same site's comparison page says 'roughly 60W', so the range is 45–60 W, or 1.08–1.44 kWh/day. The DELTA Pro Ultra X measured about 36 W idle. No byline or date on the page.

findings.label: Idle draw, second figure from the same tester
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra vs DELTA Pro Ultra X: Which Power Station is Better? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 'Nearly double the idle rate (roughly 60W)' compared with the Ultra X's 36 W. The method is not described. This conflicts with the 45 W on the site's own Ultra X review.

findings.label: AC energy drawn to fill one battery, measured
findings.value: 7.25 kWh from the wall to fill a 6 kWh battery in 4 h 4 min on 120 V
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra real-world testing (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 6.0 / 7.25 ≈ 83% charge-side efficiency (my arithmetic). The same test ran a load of 'just under 6,000 W' for 59 minutes and called it '98% efficiency'. The exact load is not given, so that figure can't be checked. It held a 9,200 W surge for about 10 s. No byline or date.

findings.label: Standby drain, owner-measured
findings.value: 72 W average (6% SoC in 12 h) to 110 W average (10% SoC in 13 h)
findings.source_title: PW3 discharges 10% overnight when in standby (Tesla Motors Club)
findings.note: Posted by Tesla Motors Club user apacheguy on 2025-04-26 and 2025-05-03, derived from SoC drop against 14.4 kWh nominal. In the same thread on 2025-04-18, user toononame reported 1.5–2 kWh/day (about 65–80 W). These are owner logs, not a lab test. 72–110 W = 1.7–2.6 kWh/day.

findings.label: Round-trip efficiency, maker spec (corrects rivals' 97.5%)
findings.value: 89% solar → battery → home/grid; 97.5% solar → home/grid (CEC weighted)
findings.note: The 89% applies at 25 °C, beginning of life, 3.3 kW charge/discharge, in a typical solar-shifting use case. EnergySage and iTechGuides list 97.5% as 'roundtrip', but per Tesla that figure is solar-to-home only. SolarQuotes (Finn Peacock) also gives 89%.

unsourced: A measured idle or standby draw for the FranklinWH aPower 2 / aGate. I searched reviewers, EnergySage and owner reports and found none.
